chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Muhammad ibn Mansur, who said:
I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about a man who vowed a vow regarding fasting, so he was unable to fulfill it. He said: 'My father used to say: Upon him, in place of each day, is a Mudd.'

key_terms.مَكَانَ: In place of / as compensation for
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific measure of volume for food, approximately 750 grams
key_terms.نَذْرٌ: A vow or promise to perform an act of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a person who vows to fast but cannot fulfill the vow?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) clarifies that the expiation for a failed vow of fasting is equivalent to the standard kaffarah for missed fasts, prescribing one Mudd of food per day. This ruling aligns with the precedent set by his father, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific vows of fasting are treated similarly to general missed fasts in terms of redemption. The use of 'Mudd' highlights the traditional measure of approximately 750 grams of staple food, emphasizing the practical application of charity in fulfilling religious obligations.
